subject: Optimize Toolkit: pilot economic scenarios & quant/batching guidance
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena@finsight.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Optimize Toolkit: pricing and pilot design for FinSight.ai

Thanks for the run-through this morning — the demo made the performance story clear. We’re evaluating Redwood’s Optimize toolkit to reduce inference spend and improve latency for our customer-support triage pipeline. A couple quick facts about our profile to help frame pricing:
- Production traffic (expected): ~100k queries/day, peak bursts at 8pm PST
- Typical prompt: median 80 tokens, 95th percentile ~120 tokens
- Mostly synchronous chat-like calls; a small portion (~15%) are large-context retrievals that would benefit from KV caching

Could you outline pilot vs committed pricing options and how batching + KV caching + quantization would change unit economics? Procurement also asked for an SOW template and any recommended acceptance tests (latency percentiles + token-cost targets).

Attaching a short SOW draft and our usage template (see attachment stub). Would like to circle back this week if possible.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Platform
FinSight.ai

Attachments: SOW_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), usage_profile_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@finsight.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pricing and pilot design for FinSight.ai

Hi Lena — really appreciate the context and the usage file. High level options below; I attached a one-page pilot pricing sketch and a blank usage template for your team to confirm numbers.

1) Short pilot (recommended)
   - Duration: 60 days
   - Prepaid credits: $10,000 in Optimize credits (apply to tokens + Optimize toolkit evaluation services)
   - Goals: validate end-to-end latency <= 250ms P95 on typical flows, 20–30% token-cost reduction via caching/batching in live traffic
   - Acceptance tests: P95 latency, token-cost delta vs baseline, regression on correctness test prompts

2) 12-month committed plan (post-pilot)
   - Commit bands: flexible tiering (3 tiers) with step discounts: 10% / 18% / 25% off list for increasing monthly committed spend
   - Additional operational credits for migration and runbook integration for larger commits

Technical levers (how they affect pricing)
   - Batching: continuous/dynamic batching reduces per-token compute cost; expect 15–35% unit savings depending on request-size distribution and max batch settings
   - KV caching (prefix/KV reuse): for chat + retrieval, KV cache can cut repeated decode steps — incremental savings of 10–30% for conversational hot-paths
   - Quantization: recommended path is model-specific — most workloads do well with int8 quantization for minimal quality loss; int4 can be an option if you accept more quality risk and lower latency/costs

Tradeoffs we should discuss on the call: latency tightness for interactive UX vs aggressive batching, and the amount of acceptable QA for int4 quantization on your retrieval-heavy flows.

I’ll loop Connor in to propose concrete commit bands and a technical checklist we can include in the SOW. I put a short pilot_pricing_sketch.pdf and a usage_profile_template.xlsx in this thread.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_pricing_sketch.pdf, usage_profile_template.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@finsight.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pricing and pilot design for FinSight.ai

Lena — quick technical follow-up with a concrete map of options (keeping things conservative for procurement):

Commercial mapping (suggested) - monthly token bands (post-pilot):
   - Tier A: 0–1M tokens/mo => list price, no discount
   - Tier B: 1–10M tokens/mo => 10% discount
   - Tier C: 10–50M tokens/mo => 18% discount
   - Tier D: 50M+ tokens/mo => 25% discount + reserved capacity option (Dedicated)
   - Pilot-to-commit credit: pilot credits (up to $10k) applied toward first invoice if you convert to a 12mo commit within 30 days of pilot completion

Technical guidance (quant + batching + KV specifics)
   - Quantization: start with int8 runtime profile for the candidate model (we run a verification harness on a holdout prompt set). Int8 typically preserves >99% of baseline metric fidelity; int4 can be explored on a per-prompt-mode basis. See attached quantization_guide.pdf stub for measured regressions by model class.
   - Batching knobs: dynamic batching with a soft max_batch_size of 8–16 for 95ms incremental decode windows; larger batch sizes (32+) amplify throughput but add tail latency — for your 250ms P95 target, 8–16 is a safe default.
   - KV caching: recommend a two-tier cache — local per-worker prefix cache + global shared hot-cache for high-reuse conversational threads. Expected real-user savings depend on cache hit-rate; share your 7-day sample and we’ll simulate expected token-savings.

Operational notes
   - SLA exceptions: Dedicated/reserved capacity allows strict latency SLAs (we can draft an SLA appendix)
   - Security/compliance: SOC2 attestation available as an addendum; data retention configuration is part of the Private deployment offering if you need tenant isolation

I can run a quick micro-benchmark if you drop a ~1k-sample of real conversation traces into the template. That will let us give a tighter savings multiplier for caching/batching.

—Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantization_guide.pdf

From: Lena Park <lena@finsight.ai>

Thanks Ben and Connor — helpful framing. Two items from our side:

1) Procurement is asking for a redline of the SOW (I attached a first-pass SOW_draft.docx). Can you:
   - Add specific acceptance criteria (latency P95 target + token-cost delta)
   - Include a clause about trial credits applying to first invoice if we convert

2) We’d like Redwood to run a short efficiency test on a representative 1k sample (anonymized); if you can give us the script/requirements we’ll share the data. Procurement also wants SOC2 and data-retention language included in the commercial appendix — can that be added to the SOW or an appendix?

If the numbers work, we want to start the pilot next week. Please send a final pilot scope and an estimated cost range for the committed bands Connor outlined.

Thanks,
Lena

Attachment: SOW_draft.docx

Commercial proposal (estimated) - If you convert to 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot completion: credits applied to month 1 invoice, and you qualify for the following discount bands (per Connor): Tier B (1–10M): 10% | Tier C (10–50M): 18% | Tier D (50M+): 25% + reserved capacity pricing available

Quant & ops notes - Start with int8 profile for the pilot; we’ll run an int4 experiment in a controlled QA bucket if you want to push further cost savings (we’ll flag potential quality deltas in the acceptance report)
 - We’ll provide a short script and anonymization checklist for the 1k-sample efficiency test (see Drive link).

I’m attaching a redlined SOW template (attached as SOW_redlined.docx stub) and a short MPA pointer. If procurement is comfortable, we can kick off on Monday and schedule a 30–45 minute tech-runbook session during week 1.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Ben Carter
